# Guard the Flock

> An independent educational and support resource for the Christian Church and faith communities to recognize, understand, and recover from spiritual abuse, discern healthy biblical leadership, and find trusted help.

## About Guard the Flock
Guard the Flock is a comprehensive resource created to help individuals, church members, and pastoral leaders understand religious coercive control and spiritual abuse. It equips readers with clear definitions, behavioral red flags, biblical discernment frameworks, practical safety and recovery steps, and documented public case studies.

## Key Sections & Direct Links
- [Understand Spiritual Abuse](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#understand): Core definitions, theological manipulation, coercive control, and the distinction between biblical guidance and spiritual coercion.
- [Warning Signs & Discernment](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#discern): Common red flags, isolation tactics, demand for unquestioned obedience, culture of fear, and distinguishing shepherd leadership from authoritarian control.
- [Get Help / Practical Steps](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#help): Practical safety guidelines, trauma-informed support services, documentation tips, and safe exit planning.
- [For Church Leaders](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#leaders): Cultivating healthy pastoral care, independent governance, accountability mechanisms, and safeguarding frameworks.
- [Documented Cases](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#cases): Case studies, independent review findings, and systemic lessons learned from public investigations across various church traditions.
- [Study & Resources](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#study): Recommended books, academic research, partner organisations, and scripture studies (including 1 Peter 5, Ezekiel 34, and Jeremiah 23).
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#faq): Clear answers regarding orthodoxy vs. abuse, confronting leadership, recovering faith after trauma, and organizational prevention.

## Biblical Foundations
- **1 Peter 5:2–3**: "Be shepherds of God's flock that is under your care, watching over them — not because you must, but because you are willing, as God wants you to be; not pursuing dishonest gain, but eager to serve; not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock."
- **Ezekiel 34**: Prophetic warning against self-serving shepherds who exploit the vulnerable rather than strengthening the weak and healing the sick.
- **Matthew 20:25–28**: Servant leadership contrasted with secular authoritarian models that lord authority over others.

## Helplines & Support Directory
The site lists professional, independent support resources for victims of spiritual and emotional abuse, including domestic abuse helplines, church safeguarding bodies, and professional therapy directories.
